_comment: Fragment 51 — D-97: second critic pass, deadlock proposal, Q11 shape accepted, POC Fn_Spec blocked one tier up. Merged 2026-08-22.

nodes.label: D-97 — The Second Critic Pass and the Deadlock Proposal
nodes.description: The critic pass condition 3 requires, run against the committed artifact set. Eight findings, none dismissed, six of them defects introduced by the two passes that were correcting the previous ones.
nodes.rationale: The correction rate is not yet below the defect-introduction rate, and that is the finding the pass most wants read.

nodes.label: Nothing Was Stopping the Critic Pass
nodes.description: The separate-turn rule was satisfied once the prior work was committed history, and Lane A kept reporting the pass as owed next turn while the qualifying turn had already arrived. The Judge asked what was stopping it and the answer was nothing.
nodes.rationale: A rule that defers correctly once will defer incorrectly forever if nobody asks when it stops applying. A correct constraint restated past the condition that made it correct is this project's dominant failure shape wearing procedural clothes.

nodes.label: Three Named Classes Each Recurred Inside Their Own Fix
nodes.description: A restated tally reappeared as a section heading naming a count above a table of five. A wrong anchor reappeared in the pass that corrected wrong anchors. A stale commit pin reappeared after the artifact set moved twice.
nodes.rationale: Six of the second pass's eight findings are defects introduced by correcting passes. Naming a class and fixing one instance does not retire the class.

nodes.label: A Clean Bill of Health That Ages Into a False Claim
nodes.description: The first pass recorded that it found nothing about the checks, the graph or the lane map, and called that the controls working. Within a day the manifest check was silently dropping rows and the config coupling check was entirely uninstalled.
nodes.rationale: Withdrawn rather than deleted, because a weakness must leave evidence. It is worse than no statement because it tells the next reader a region has been examined when it has not. Not examined is not the same as sound.

nodes.label: The Deadlock Proposal — Close Phase 1 on What Orchestration Owed
nodes.description: Close Phase 1 on its orchestration artifacts and move the remaining configuration implementation into Phase 2's opening scope, carrying the red coupling check explicitly as opening debt rather than silencing it.
nodes.rationale: Authorizing a lane to act inside an unopened phase legitimises exactly the earlier defect, and once phase order admits a just-this-once the exception becomes the procedure. The cost is stated: sprints and phases decouple again, which is a partial re-adoption of the position the ruling rejected.

nodes.label: A Condition That Demands Work Its Own Lane May Not Touch
nodes.description: Condition 5 as first written required a phase to finish implementation that belongs to a different lane. The scoping error was Lane A's reading of the ruling, not the ruling itself.
nodes.rationale: Phase 1 is the orchestration phase and orchestration's sprint duty was to publish authoritative configuration rows, which it did. Implementation was never Phase 1's to complete.

nodes.label: Q11 Shape Decided — Three Values, Not a Boolean
nodes.description: The column carries satisfied, not_applicable and override_not_four_eyes as the functional requirement already states. A crossing boolean, if wanted, is a derived view and never a stored duplicate. The naming half of the question stays open.
nodes.rationale: Arithmetic rather than preference: the metric excludes logged overrides, which needs two of the three values distinguishable, and a boolean maps both to false. Deciding the rename here would read approval of one half as approval of both.

nodes.label: C-23 Closed Exactly as Written
nodes.description: Two stale claims in the product requirements decision row were reported by the build lane and deliberately left standing for a full cycle, then corrected in the same pass the decision landed.
nodes.rationale: Rewriting an open decision request is answering it by edit. The restraint is what made the correction safe rather than pre-emptive, and the condition was written to close this way.

nodes.label: An Fn_Spec Cannot Be Written Without a Feature Group Above It
nodes.description: The POC has no feature group in the product requirements document — one changelog mention, no functional requirement, no user story, no acceptance criterion. Writing a functional specification from prose produces unanchored scope.
nodes.rationale: The binding guardrail requires a feature group as input, never a prose description, because anchors travel with the input. So proceeding to the functional-specification tier necessarily includes adding a feature group to the governed product spec, which is a larger act than the instruction's phrasing implies.
